'''''Plectranthus fruticosus''''', the '''forest spurflower''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the mint [[family (botany)|family]], [[Lamiaceae]]. It is [[native species|native]] to [[Mozambique]], [[Eswatini]], and [[South Africa]]'s [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[Northern Provinces|Northern]], and [[Cape Provinces|Cape]] provinces.<ref name = powo>[https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:454404-1 ''Plectranthus fruticosus'' L'Hér.] ''[[Plants of the World Online]]''. Retrieved 25 September 2023.</ref> Growing up to {{convert|2|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall, it is an erect [[evergreen]] shrub, with rounded, hairy leaves, and spikes of soft blue or mauve flowers in summer.

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''fruticosus'' means "shrubby".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=184533731X }}</ref>

This plant is found throughout the Western Cape and Limpopo regions, enjoying the moist conditions and dappled shade of forest margins.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.theplantlibrary.co.za/Plants/Plectranthus-fruticosus
| title = Plectranthus fruticosus  | publisher = The Plant Library | access-date = 3 May 2018}}</ref>

It has a long history of cultivation in Europe, where it requires protection from freezing temperatures. Several [[cultivar]]s are available, of which the pink-flowered 'James' has won the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/166961/Plectranthus-fruticosus-James/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Plectranthus fruticosus'' 'James' | access-date = 2 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 79 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 2 May 2018}}</ref>
